column9: Earning by your own work: 掙錢, 掙工資. 掙錢 is northern speech; 賺錢 is used everywhere.

column3: To make money by working: 挣钱养家 "earn to support a family", 挣钱不容易. 挣 stresses the effort of working for it, while 赚钱 is wider and also covers profit from trading. Spoken, and the usual word for ordinary wages. 钱 has 钅 for the metal of coins.
column4: 他每天辛苦地挣钱养家。
column5: 他每天辛苦地掙錢養家。
column6: Tā měitiān xīnkǔ de zhèngqián yǎngjiā.
column7: He works hard every day to earn money for his family.
column9: To make money by working: 掙錢養家 "earn to support a family", 掙錢不容易. 掙 stresses the effort of working for it, while 賺錢 is wider and also covers profit from trading. Spoken, and the usual word for ordinary wages. 錢 has 釒 for the metal of coins.

column3: Benefits from a job or the state: 员工福利, 社会福利, 福利好 (good perks).
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de fúlì hěn hǎo.
column7: This company has very good benefits.
column9: Benefits from a job or the state: 員工福利, 社會福利, 福利好 (good perks).

column3: Funds for an organization or project, not a person’s own money: 研究经费, 经费不足. Personal spending money is just 钱; costs are 费用.
column6: Xuéxiào de jīngfèi bù gòu yòng.
column7: The school's funds are not enough.
column9: Funds for an organization or project, not a person’s own money: 研究經費, 經費不足. Personal spending money is just 錢; costs are 費用.

column3: Money support for a person or cause, such as school or research: 资助学生. The person helped is the object: 资助他上大学. Help of any kind is 帮助.
column6: Yǒurén zīzhù tā shàng dàxué.
column7: Someone is paying for him to go to university.
column9: Money support for a person or cause, such as school or research: 資助學生. The person helped is the object: 資助他上大學. Help of any kind is 幫助.

column3: Both a noun and a verb, and the opposite of 收入; the two together are 收支, income and expenses. Typical nouns around it are 每月支出, 减少支出, 日常支出.
column4: 我们每个月的支出很大。
column5: 我們每個月的支出很大。
column6: Wǒmen měi ge yuè de zhīchū hěn dà.
column7: Our monthly spending is large.
column9: Both a noun and a verb, and the opposite of 收入; the two together are 收支, income and expenses. Typical nouns around it are 每月支出, 減少支出, 日常支出.

column3: Mostly met in compounds such as 罚款 and 处罚, but in speech it works alone with an amount or a punishment: 罚钱, 罚了他两百块, 罚站 (make someone stand as punishment).
column6: Tā chídào le, bèi fá le.
column7: He was late and got fined.
column9: Mostly met in compounds such as 罰款 and 處罰, but in speech it works alone with an amount or a punishment: 罰錢, 罰了他兩百塊, 罰站 (make someone stand as punishment).

column3: Works as a verb and as a noun. The person fined is the subject of 被罚款, or you pay the noun with 交: 交罚款, 罚款两百元. The verb already contains its object, so the amount follows 罚款, not a second object.
column6: Tā luàn tíng chē bèi fákuǎn le.
column7: He was fined for parking illegally.
column9: Works as a verb and as a noun. The person fined is the subject of 被罰款, or you pay the noun with 交: 交罰款, 罰款兩百元. The verb already contains its object, so the amount follows 罰款, not a second object.

column3: Mainly a business losing money: 亏钱, 亏本, 亏了五万; the opposite is 赚. Two other uses are common in speech: 多亏你, thanks to you, and an ironic 亏你说得出口, how can you say that.
column6: Zhè bǐ shēngyi wǒ kuī le.
column7: I lost money on this deal.
column9: Mainly a business losing money: 虧錢, 虧本, 虧了五萬; the opposite is 賺. Two other uses are common in speech: 多虧你, thanks to you, and an ironic 虧你說得出口, how can you say that.

column3: A written word for 没(有) with 过: 不曾见过, 不曾想到. It denies an experience that did not happen, so it is never used for a habit. 曾 began as a picture of a cooker for steaming food and was later borrowed, for its sound, to write the word for once already.
column6: Wǒ cónglái bùcéng jiàn guo tā.
column7: I have never seen him.
column9: A written word for 沒(有) with 過: 不曾見過, 不曾想到. It denies an experience that did not happen, so it is never used for a habit. 曾 began as a picture of a cooker for steaming food and was later borrowed, for its sound, to write the word for once already.

column3: Goes before the verb for something that repeats at no fixed moment, a little more often than 偶尔: 不时看手机. In the set phrase 不时之需 it means a need that may arise at any moment.
column6: Tā bùshí kàn yīxià shǒujī.
column7: He looks at his phone from time to time.
column9: Goes before the verb for something that repeats at no fixed moment, a little more often than 偶爾: 不時看手機. In the set phrase 不時之需 it means a need that may arise at any moment.

column3: Before a verb it takes 地: 不停地说. After a verb it follows 个, which adds a feeling of too much: 下个不停, 笑个不停. To stop, in the sense of ending an action, is 停下来.
column6: Yǔ xià ge bùtíng.
column7: It keeps raining without stopping.
column9: Before a verb it takes 地: 不停地說. After a verb it follows 個, which adds a feeling of too much: 下個不停, 笑個不停. To stop, in the sense of ending an action, is 停下來.

column3: Goes before the verb like 常常, but sounds more written and is less common in conversation: 时常想起, 时常联系.
column6: Tā shícháng gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
column7: He often calls me.
column9: Goes before the verb like 常常, but sounds more written and is less common in conversation: 時常想起, 時常聯繫.

column3: Goes before the verb and speaks of how often: rarely, once in a while. Do not use it for chance: that is 偶然, as in 偶然遇到, which says it was not planned.
column6: Wǒ ǒu'ěr qù nà jiā kāfēiguǎn.
column7: I go to that café once in a while.
column9: Goes before the verb and speaks of how often: rarely, once in a while. Do not use it for chance: that is 偶然, as in 偶然遇到, which says it was not planned.

column3: Works as an adjective (这是偶然的) and as an adverb before a verb (偶然发现). The opposite is 必然, inevitable. The ending 然 turns many words into adverbs, as in 突然 and 忽然.
column6: Wǒmen shì ǒurán rènshi de.
column7: We got to know each other by chance.
column9: Works as an adjective (這是偶然的) and as an adverb before a verb (偶然發現). The opposite is 必然, inevitable. The ending 然 turns many words into adverbs, as in 突然 and 忽然.

column3: Only for a habit or state that has held until now: 他一向很准时, 我一向不吃辣. It sits before a verb or adjective, often with 很 or a negative, and is not used for a single event or the future.
column6: Tā yīxiàng hěn zhǔnshí.
column7: He has always been punctual.
column9: Only for a habit or state that has held until now: 他一向很準時, 我一向不吃辣. It sits before a verb or adjective, often with 很 or a negative, and is not used for a single event or the future.

column3: Still, as before, in writing, often looking back with some feeling: 风景依旧 "the scenery is unchanged", 依旧如此. It says that something stayed the same after a change or after time passed. 依 "rely on" has the sound part 衣, which sounds just the same, yī.
column4: 十年后，他依旧住在这里。
column5: 十年後，他依舊住在這裡。
column6: Shí nián hòu, tā yījiù zhù zài zhèlǐ.
column7: Ten years later, he still lives here.
column9: Still, as before, in writing, often looking back with some feeling: 風景依舊 "the scenery is unchanged", 依舊如此. It says that something stayed the same after a change or after time passed. 依 "rely on" has the sound part 衣, which sounds just the same, yī.

column3: Still, as before: 仍旧坚持, 仍旧没有变. Much like 依旧, though 仍旧 usually describes an action or situation going on in spite of the change around it. 仍然 is the common spoken form. 仍 has 亻 and 乃, whose sound it follows.
column4: 虽然很累，他仍旧坚持工作。
column5: 雖然很累，他仍舊堅持工作。
column6: Suīrán hěn lèi, tā réngjiù jiānchí gōngzuò.
column7: Although he was tired, he kept on working.
column9: Still, as before: 仍舊堅持, 仍舊沒有變. Much like 依舊, though 仍舊 usually describes an action or situation going on in spite of the change around it. 仍然 is the common spoken form. 仍 has 亻 and 乃, whose sound it follows.

column3: A more formal way to say one more time, placed before the verb and fine for past or future: 再次强调, 再次见面. In plain speech 再 looks ahead and 又 reports what has already happened again.
column4: 他再次向大家表示感谢。
column5: 他再次向大家表示感謝。
column6: Tā zàicì xiàng dàjiā biǎoshì gǎnxiè.
column7: He thanked everyone once more.
column9: A more formal way to say one more time, placed before the verb and fine for past or future: 再次強調, 再次見面. In plain speech 再 looks ahead and 又 reports what has already happened again.

column3: Always followed by a negative: 再也不, 再也没有, 再也不能. It is stronger than 不再, saying that something has ended for good. It goes before the verb: 他再也没回来.
column6: Wǒ zàiyě bù xiǎng chī le.
column7: I never want to eat that again.
column9: Always followed by a negative: 再也不, 再也沒有, 再也不能. It is stronger than 不再, saying that something has ended for good. It goes before the verb: 他再也沒回來.

column3: Opens a clause, and the result usually follows with 就: 一旦开始，就不要放弃. It is used for an event that, once it happens, changes things, often something bad or important: 一旦发生.
column6: Yīdàn kāishǐ, jiù bùyào fàngqì.
column7: Once you start, do not give up.
column9: Opens a clause, and the result usually follows with 就: 一旦開始，就不要放棄. It is used for an event that, once it happens, changes things, often something bad or important: 一旦發生.

column3: Titles are built as unit plus 长: 局长, 校长, 市长, 厂长. Add the department to name a particular post: 公安局长, 邮政局长. In a title 长 is read zhǎng, but when it means long it is read cháng.
column6: Júzhǎng zhèngzài kāihuì.
column7: The bureau chief is in a meeting.
column9: Titles are built as unit plus 長: 局長, 校長, 市長, 廠長. Add the department to name a particular post: 公安局長, 郵政局長. In a title 長 is read zhǎng, but when it means long it is read cháng.

column3: Built like 局长 and 校长: the place plus 长. People say it as a form of address too: 厂长，您好. In a title 长 is read zhǎng, but when it means long it is read cháng.
column6: Chǎngzhǎng jīntiān yào lái jiǎnchá.
column7: The factory director is coming to inspect today.
column9: Built like 局長 and 校長: the place plus 長. People say it as a form of address too: 廠長，您好. In a title 長 is read zhǎng, but when it means long it is read cháng.

column3: The leader of any 团, and the context tells you which kind: a tour (旅游团团长), a delegation, a performing troupe, or an army regiment. Online it is also the organizer of a group purchase. In a title 长 is read zhǎng, but when it means long it is read cháng.
column4: 团长带我们参观了博物馆。
column5: 團長帶我們參觀了博物館。
column6: Tuánzhǎng dài wǒmen cānguān le bówùguǎn.
column7: The group leader took us around the museum.
column9: The leader of any 團, and the context tells you which kind: a tour (旅遊團團長), a delegation, a performing troupe, or an army regiment. Online it is also the organizer of a group purchase. In a title 長 is read zhǎng, but when it means long it is read cháng.

column3: A respectful way to call a skilled worker such as a driver, repairman or cook, and a word for the master of a craft or of martial arts. 师傅，请问… is how you stop a driver to ask something.
column4: 师傅，请问去火车站怎么走？
column5: 師傅，請問去火車站怎麼走？
column6: Shīfu, qǐngwèn qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu?
column7: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?
column9: A respectful way to call a skilled worker such as a driver, repairman or cook, and a word for the master of a craft or of martial arts. 師傅，請問… is how you stop a driver to ask something.

column3: The field names the post: 法律顾问, 技术顾问, 财务顾问. You hire one with 聘请顾问, or work as one with 当顾问. A consulting firm is a 顾问公司 or 咨询公司.
column6: Tā shì gōngsī de fǎlǜ gùwèn.
column7: He is the company's legal adviser.
column9: The field names the post: 法律顧問, 技術顧問, 財務顧問. You hire one with 聘請顧問, or work as one with 當顧問. A consulting firm is a 顧問公司 or 咨詢公司.

column3: A title for someone who assists a senior person: 经理助理, 行政助理. It is also a rank in 助理教授, assistant professor. For plain help with a task, 助手 is the word.
column6: Tā shì jīnglǐ de zhùlǐ.
column7: She is the manager's assistant.
column9: A title for someone who assists a senior person: 經理助理, 行政助理. It is also a rank in 助理教授, assistant professor. For plain help with a task, 助手 is the word.

column3: A helper by role, not a job title, unlike 助理: 得力助手, a researcher's or a doctor's helper. 手 stands for a person doing certain work, as in 歌手 and 选手.
column4: 我需要一个助手帮我整理资料。
column5: 我需要一個助手幫我整理資料。
column6: Wǒ xūyào yī ge zhùshǒu bāng wǒ zhěnglǐ zīliào.
column7: I need an assistant to help me organize the material.
column9: A helper by role, not a job title, unlike 助理: 得力助手, a researcher's or a doctor's helper. 手 stands for a person doing certain work, as in 歌手 and 選手.

column3: The president or chief executive of a large company or bank: 集团总裁, 副总裁 "vice president". The 总裁 runs the business, while the 董事长 "chairman" leads the board (董事会), which decides and oversees. 裁 has 衣 "clothing" and 戈, and means to cut cloth, hence "decide", as in 裁判 and 裁员.
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā jítuán de zǒngcái.
column7: He is the chief executive of this group.
column9: The president or chief executive of a large company or bank: 集團總裁, 副總裁 "vice president". The 總裁 runs the business, while the 董事長 "chairman" leads the board (董事會), which decides and oversees. 裁 has 衣 "clothing" and 戈, and means to cut cloth, hence "decide", as in 裁判 and 裁員.

column3: Three uses: the noun for your supervisor (我的主管, 部门主管), a verb for being in charge of an area (主管销售), and before a noun for the responsible body (主管部门).
column6: Wǒ de zhǔguǎn jīntiān bù zài.
column7: My supervisor is not in today.
column9: Three uses: the noun for your supervisor (我的主管, 部門主管), a verb for being in charge of an area (主管銷售), and before a noun for the responsible body (主管部門).

column3: The verb 负责 plus 人 names the one who is responsible: 项目负责人, 公司负责人. Asking 负责人是谁 is how you find who is in charge. The -人 ending works the same in 联系人 and 发言人.
column4: 请问这里的负责人是谁？
column5: 請問這裡的負責人是誰？
column6: Qǐngwèn zhèlǐ de fùzérén shì shéi?
column7: Excuse me, who is in charge here?
column9: The verb 負責 plus 人 names the one who is responsible: 項目負責人, 公司負責人. Asking 負責人是誰 is how you find who is in charge. The -人 ending works the same in 聯繫人 and 發言人.

column3: The academic degree and its holder, not a physician: a medical doctor is 医生. It follows a surname as a title (王博士), and 博士生 is a doctoral student. The usual verb is 读: 读博士.
column6: Tā zài Měiguó dú bóshì.
column7: She is studying for a doctorate in America.
column9: The academic degree and its holder, not a physician: a medical doctor is 醫生. It follows a surname as a title (王博士), and 博士生 is a doctoral student. The usual verb is 讀: 讀博士.

column3: The middle degree: 学士, 硕士, 博士. You study for it (读硕士) and finish it (硕士毕业); 硕士学位 is the degree itself.
column6: Tā jīnnián shuòshì bìyè.
column7: He finishes his master's degree this year.
column9: The middle degree: 學士, 碩士, 博士. You study for it (讀碩士) and finish it (碩士畢業); 碩士學位 is the degree itself.

column3: Someone who studies a field seriously, often with a field word: 著名学者, 历史学者. The ending 者 means the person who does it, as in 记者, 作者 and 消费者. A pupil is 学生, not 学者.
column4: 这位学者研究古代历史。
column5: 這位學者研究古代歷史。
column6: Zhè wèi xuézhě yánjiū gǔdài lìshǐ.
column7: This scholar studies ancient history.
column9: Someone who studies a field seriously, often with a field word: 著名學者, 歷史學者. The ending 者 means the person who does it, as in 記者, 作者 and 消費者. A pupil is 學生, not 學者.

column3: Stresses the seat in the organization and its rank: 高级职位, a job opening in 招聘职位, or what you do when you 申请职位. For the duties that come with it, 职务.
column4: 他在公司里的职位很高。
column5: 他在公司裡的職位很高。
column6: Tā zài gōngsī lǐ de zhíwèi hěn gāo.
column7: He holds a high position in the company.
column9: Stresses the seat in the organization and its rank: 高級職位, a job opening in 招聘職位, or what you do when you 申請職位. For the duties that come with it, 職務.

column3: Stresses the task and title that come with a job, in formal announcements: 担任职务, 免去职务. 你担任什么职务 is the formal way to ask what someone's post is. For the rank itself, 职位.
column4: 他在公司担任什么职务？
column5: 他在公司擔任什麼職務？
column6: Tā zài gōngsī dānrèn shénme zhíwù?
column7: What post does he hold in the company?
column9: Stresses the task and title that come with a job, in formal announcements: 擔任職務, 免去職務. 你擔任什麼職務 is the formal way to ask what someone's post is. For the rank itself, 職位.

column3: Mostly physical work: 体力劳动. As a noun it also names work as a value (热爱劳动), and 劳动节 is May Day. For an office job, say 工作 instead.
column4: 学生们在学校参加劳动。
column5: 學生們在學校參加勞動。
column6: Xuéshengmen zài xuéxiào cānjiā láodòng.
column7: The students take part in labor at school.
column9: Mostly physical work: 體力勞動. As a noun it also names work as a value (熱愛勞動), and 勞動節 is May Day. For an office job, say 工作 instead.

column3: Treats people as a resource to count, not as individuals: 人力不足, 节省人力, 人力资源 (human resources). Paired with 物力 it gives 人力物力, people and material.
column4: 这项工作需要很多人力。
column5: 這項工作需要很多人力。
column6: Zhè xiàng gōngzuò xūyào hěn duō rénlì.
column7: This job needs a lot of manpower.
column9: Treats people as a resource to count, not as individuals: 人力不足, 節省人力, 人力資源 (human resources). Paired with 物力 it gives 人力物力, people and material.

column3: The object is something sizable, such as a competition, a conference or the Olympics. Posters name the organizer with 由…主办 or list it as 主办单位, next to the 承办单位 that does the work.
column6: Zhè cì bǐsài yóu xuéxiào zhǔbàn.
column7: This competition is hosted by the school.
column9: The object is something sizable, such as a competition, a conference or the Olympics. Posters name the organizer with 由…主辦 or list it as 主辦單位, next to the 承辦單位 that does the work.

column3: The 主办 side owns the event and hands it over; the 承办 side takes it on and does the work. You see it in 由…承办 and 承办方 on posters and notices.
column4: 这个活动由一家公司承办。
column5: 這個活動由一家公司承辦。
column6: Zhège huódòng yóu yī jiā gōngsī chéngbàn.
column7: A company is running this event.
column9: The 主辦 side owns the event and hands it over; the 承辦 side takes it on and does the work. You see it in 由…承辦 and 承辦方 on posters and notices.

column3: A formal word for following through on something already decided: an order, plan, task or law, as in 执行任务 and 严格执行. 执行力 is the ability to get things done.
column4: 大家必须严格执行这个规定。
column5: 大家必須嚴格執行這個規定。
column6: Dàjiā bìxū yángé zhíxíng zhège guīdìng.
column7: Everyone must strictly carry out this rule.
column9: A formal word for following through on something already decided: an order, plan, task or law, as in 執行任務 and 嚴格執行. 執行力 is the ability to get things done.

column3: As a verb the object is usually people or an event, and the organizer is the subject: 组织学生, 组织活动. As a noun it covers any formal body, from 联合国 agencies to 非政府组织.
column4: 学校组织学生去参观博物馆。
column5: 學校組織學生去參觀博物館。
column6: Xuéxiào zǔzhī xuésheng qù cānguān bówùguǎn.
column7: The school organized the students to visit a museum.
column9: As a verb the object is usually people or an event, and the organizer is the subject: 組織學生, 組織活動. As a noun it covers any formal body, from 聯合國 agencies to 非政府組織.

column3: For a first founding of something important or lasting: 创立公司, 创立学派, 创立理论. 建立 is wider and also fits setting up relations or systems.
column4: 他三十年前创立了这家公司。
column5: 他三十年前創立了這家公司。
column6: Tā sānshí nián qián chuànglì le zhè jiā gōngsī.
column7: He founded this company thirty years ago.
column9: For a first founding of something important or lasting: 創立公司, 創立學派, 創立理論. 建立 is wider and also fits setting up relations or systems.

column3: A verb plus its object, so other words slip in: 值了一天班, 值夜班. A room kept for it is 值班室, and 今天谁值班 asks whose turn it is.
column6: Jīnwǎn lúndào wǒ zhíbān.
column7: Tonight it is my turn on duty.
column9: A verb plus its object, so other words slip in: 值了一天班, 值夜班. A room kept for it is 值班室, and 今天誰值班 asks whose turn it is.

column3: A verb plus its object, so 辞了职 and 辞去职务 are normal; the letter is 辞职信. It is quitting by choice. Being fired is 被开除.
column4: 他决定辞职，自己做生意。
column5: 他決定辭職，自己做生意。
column6: Tā juédìng cízhí, zìjǐ zuò shēngyi.
column7: He decided to quit and run his own business.
column9: A verb plus its object, so 辭了職 and 辭去職務 are normal; the letter is 辭職信. It is quitting by choice. Being fired is 被開除.

column3: What a body is meant to do, not what a person's job is: 政府职能, 职能部门, 职能转变. The subject is an office, department or government.
column4: 这个部门的职能是管理市场。
column5: 這個部門的職能是管理市場。
column6: Zhège bùmén de zhínéng shì guǎnlǐ shìchǎng.
column7: The function of this department is to manage the market.
column9: What a body is meant to do, not what a person's job is: 政府職能, 職能部門, 職能轉變. The subject is an office, department or government.

column3: A verb plus object with the school as subject and the number after it. Related: 招生简章 (admissions brochure) and 招生办. 招 is to recruit, as in 招聘, and 生 here is a student.
column4: 这所学校今年招生三百人。
column5: 這所學校今年招生三百人。
column6: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào jīnnián zhāoshēng sānbǎi rén.
column7: This school enrolls three hundred students this year.
column9: A verb plus object with the school as subject and the number after it. Related: 招生簡章 (admissions brochure) and 招生辦. 招 is to recruit, as in 招聘, and 生 here is a student.

column3: The formal word for providing an organization with equipment or staff: 配备人员, 配备电脑. The place or unit is the subject or topic. As a noun it is the equipment provided; 装备 is gear for troops or expeditions.
column4: 每个教室都配备了电脑。
column5: 每個教室都配備了電腦。
column6: Měi ge jiàoshì dōu pèibèi le diànnǎo.
column7: Every classroom is equipped with computers.
column9: The formal word for providing an organization with equipment or staff: 配備人員, 配備電腦. The place or unit is the subject or topic. As a noun it is the equipment provided; 裝備 is gear for troops or expeditions.

column3: A colloquial all-purpose verb that stands in for a more exact one: 搞清楚, 搞错, 搞定, 搞活动. Sometimes it hints at something not quite proper, as in 搞破坏 and 搞鬼.
column6: Tā zài gǎo yī ge xīn xiàngmù.
column7: He is working on a new project.
column9: A colloquial all-purpose verb that stands in for a more exact one: 搞清楚, 搞錯, 搞定, 搞活動. Sometimes it hints at something not quite proper, as in 搞破壞 and 搞鬼.

column3: The verb 搞 plus the result 好, so 得 and 不 fit in the middle: 搞得好, 搞不好. Typical objects are 关系, 工作 and 卫生. 搞不好 also means quite possibly: 搞不好会下雨.
column6: Wǒmen yào gǎohǎo tuánduì hézuò.
column7: We must make teamwork go well.
column9: The verb 搞 plus the result 好, so 得 and 不 fit in the middle: 搞得好, 搞不好. Typical objects are 關係, 工作 and 衛生. 搞不好 also means quite possibly: 搞不好會下雨.

column3: A verb plus its object, so 动了手 and 动手做 are normal. 自己动手 is do it yourself. In a quarrel 不要动手 means no hitting, and 请勿动手 on a sign means do not touch.
column4: 遇到问题，我们自己动手解决。
column5: 遇到問題，我們自己動手解決。
column6: Yùdào wèntí, wǒmen zìjǐ dòngshǒu jiějué.
column7: When we meet a problem, we solve it ourselves.
column9: A verb plus its object, so 動了手 and 動手做 are normal. 自己動手 is do it yourself. In a quarrel 不要動手 means no hitting, and 請勿動手 on a sign means do not touch.

column3: The formal, large-scale word, between companies or countries: 国际贸易, 对外贸易, 贸易战. In speech, business and deals are 买卖. The 易 here is exchange, as in 交易, not the easy of 容易.
column4: 两国之间的贸易越来越多。
column5: 兩國之間的貿易越來越多。
column6: Liǎng guó zhījiān de màoyì yuèláiyuè duō.
column7: Trade between the two countries keeps growing.
column9: The formal, large-scale word, between companies or countries: 國際貿易, 對外貿易, 貿易戰. In speech, business and deals are 買賣. The 易 here is exchange, as in 交易, not the easy of 容易.

column3: Goes with 申请专利, 获得专利 and 专利权. Figuratively it is an exclusive privilege: 这不是谁的专利 says it is nobody's monopoly.
column4: 这项技术已经申请了专利。
column5: 這項技術已經申請了專利。
column6: Zhè xiàng jìshù yǐjīng shēnqǐng le zhuānlì.
column7: A patent has already been applied for on this technology.
column9: Goes with 申請專利, 獲得專利 and 專利權. Figuratively it is an exclusive privilege: 這不是誰的專利 says it is nobody's monopoly.

column3: Money put into a business: 投入资本, 资本家, 资本主义. Figuratively it is something to rely on: 他有骄傲的资本 says he has reason to be proud. 本 is the base amount, as in 本钱.
column4: 开公司需要足够的资本。
column5: 開公司需要足夠的資本。
column6: Kāi gōngsī xūyào zúgòu de zīběn.
column7: Starting a company takes enough capital.
column9: Money put into a business: 投入資本, 資本家, 資本主義. Figuratively it is something to rely on: 他有驕傲的資本 says he has reason to be proud. 本 is the base amount, as in 本錢.

column3: Everything a company or person owns, as counted on a balance sheet: 固定资产, 总资产. It differs from 资本, the money put in. For a person's own things, 财产 is the more everyday word.
column4: 这家公司的资产超过五亿元。
column5: 這家公司的資產超過五億元。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de zīchǎn chāoguò wǔ yì yuán.
column7: This company has assets of over five hundred million yuan.
column9: Everything a company or person owns, as counted on a balance sheet: 固定資產, 總資產. It differs from 資本, the money put in. For a person's own things, 財產 is the more everyday word.

column3: Three uses: an investment fund (买基金), a foundation (基金会), and a sum set aside for a purpose (教育基金).
column4: 他把一部分钱买了基金。
column5: 他把一部分錢買了基金。
column6: Tā bǎ yī bùfen qián mǎi le jījīn.
column7: He put part of his money into a fund.
column9: Three uses: an investment fund (買基金), a foundation (基金會), and a sum set aside for a purpose (教育基金).

column3: A business's profit: 利润率, 赚取利润, 利润增长. It is what is left after costs (成本). A person's earnings are 收入, not 利润. 润 means moist or to moisten, and it also has the sense profit.
column4: 公司今年的利润增长了两成。
column5: 公司今年的利潤增長了兩成。
column6: Gōngsī jīnnián de lìrùn zēngzhǎng le liǎng chéng.
column7: The company's profit grew by twenty percent this year.
column9: A business's profit: 利潤率, 賺取利潤, 利潤增長. It is what is left after costs (成本). A person's earnings are 收入, not 利潤. 潤 means moist or to moisten, and it also has the sense profit.

column3: The cost to the maker or seller: 生产成本, 降低成本. The price a buyer pays is 价格. It stretches to effort too: 时间成本. 本 is the base amount, as in 本钱.
column4: 原料涨价，生产成本也高了。
column5: 原料漲價，生產成本也高了。
column6: Yuánliào zhǎngjià, shēngchǎn chéngběn yě gāo le.
column7: Raw materials went up in price, so production costs rose too.
column9: The cost to the maker or seller: 生產成本, 降低成本. The price a buyer pays is 價格. It stretches to effort too: 時間成本. 本 is the base amount, as in 本錢.

column3: Formal, for the results of measures, policies or work, and nearly always good news: 成效显著, 取得成效, 见成效. A bad outcome is 后果.
column4: 这项政策已经取得了明显的成效。
column5: 這項政策已經取得了明顯的成效。
column6: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè yǐjīng qǔdé le míngxiǎn de chéngxiào.
column7: This policy has already achieved clear results.
column9: Formal, for the results of measures, policies or work, and nearly always good news: 成效顯著, 取得成效, 見成效. A bad outcome is 後果.

column3: The work a firm or a trade deals with: 开展业务, 熟悉业务, 业务能力 for professional skill, and 业务员 for a salesperson. The company itself is 公司, never 业务.
column4: 他对公司的业务很熟悉。
column5: 他對公司的業務很熟悉。
column6: Tā duì gōngsī de yèwù hěn shúxī.
column7: He knows the company's business well.
column9: The work a firm or a trade deals with: 開展業務, 熟悉業務, 業務能力 for professional skill, and 業務員 for a salesperson. The company itself is 公司, never 業務.

column3: A whole sector of the economy: 第三产业 is the service sector, and 产业链 the industrial chain. It is wider than 工业, which is manufacturing. Less often it means property owned: 他留下了一大笔产业.
column4: 旅游是这个城市的主要产业。
column5: 旅遊是這個城市的主要產業。
column6: Lǚyóu shì zhège chéngshì de zhǔyào chǎnyè.
column7: Tourism is this city's main industry.
column9: A whole sector of the economy: 第三產業 is the service sector, and 產業鏈 the industrial chain. It is wider than 工業, which is manufacturing. Less often it means property owned: 他留下了一大筆產業.

column3: On the mainland the apartment complex's management company, whom residents call for repairs, cleaning and security: 物业费, 联系物业. In Taiwan residents call the building's 管理员 or 管理室 instead, and 物业 mostly means real estate.
column6: Shuǐguǎn huài le, qǐng liánxì wùyè.
column7: The water pipe is broken, please contact the property management.
column9: On the mainland the apartment complex's management company, whom residents call for repairs, cleaning and security: 物業費, 聯繫物業. In Taiwan residents call the building's 管理員 or 管理室 instead, and 物業 mostly means real estate.

column3: A corporate group of many companies: 集团公司 is the parent firm, and the word sits in company names. It can also mean a bloc, as in 军事集团.
column4: 这个集团在很多国家都有工厂。
column5: 這個集團在很多國家都有工廠。
column6: Zhège jítuán zài hěn duō guójiā dōu yǒu gōngchǎng.
column7: This group has factories in many countries.
column9: A corporate group of many companies: 集團公司 is the parent firm, and the word sits in company names. It can also mean a bloc, as in 軍事集團.

column3: To act for someone: 代理人 is an agent, 代理经理 an acting manager, 代理商 a distributor. In computing it is a proxy. The same 理 as in 经理 and 助理. 理 first meant to polish jade, and its sense of ordering and tidying may come from that.
column4: 经理出差了，由副经理代理。
column5: 經理出差了，由副經理代理。
column6: Jīnglǐ chūchāi le, yóu fùjīnglǐ dàilǐ.
column7: The manager is away, so the deputy manager is acting for him.
column9: To act for someone: 代理人 is an agent, 代理經理 an acting manager, 代理商 a distributor. In computing it is a proxy. The same 理 as in 經理 and 助理. 理 first meant to polish jade, and its sense of ordering and tidying may come from that.

column3: Both to write back and the reply itself. As a verb the person comes first: 给他回信, never 回信他. Its pair is 来信, a letter that has come to you. 回 began as a picture of rotation, originally a spiral.
column6: Tā hěn kuài jiù huíxìn le.
column7: He wrote back very quickly.
column9: Both to write back and the reply itself. As a verb the person comes first: 給他回信, never 回信他. Its pair is 來信, a letter that has come to you. 回 began as a picture of rotation, originally a spiral.

column3: A letter that has come to you, seen from the receiver's side: 读者来信, 收到你的来信, 欢迎来信 in an ad. As a verb it means to write to the speaker. The reply is 回信.
column4: 我今天收到了他的来信。
column5: 我今天收到了他的來信。
column6: Wǒ jīntiān shōudào le tā de láixìn.
column7: I received a letter from him today.
column9: A letter that has come to you, seen from the receiver's side: 讀者來信, 收到你的來信, 歡迎來信 in an ad. As a verb it means to write to the speaker. The reply is 回信.

column3: A quick informal note on a slip of paper, such as one left for a roommate: 留便条, 写便条, 一张便条. It is not a formal letter.
column4: 他在桌上留了一张便条。
column5: 他在桌上留了一張便條。
column6: Tā zài zhuō shàng liú le yī zhāng biàntiáo.
column7: He left a note on the table.
column9: A quick informal note on a slip of paper, such as one left for a roommate: 留便條, 寫便條, 一張便條. It is not a formal letter.

column3: A notice about one particular matter, posted on a door or placed in a paper: 招聘启事 for a job, 寻人启事 for a missing person. It states one matter or asks the public for something: hiring, a lost item, a missing person. A 公告 announces a formal decision or rule. One scholar reads 启 as a hand opening a door.
column6: Ménkǒu tiēzhe yī zhāng qǐshì.
column7: A notice is posted at the door.
column9: A notice about one particular matter, posted on a door or placed in a paper: 招聘啟事 for a job, 尋人啟事 for a missing person. It states one matter or asks the public for something: hiring, a lost item, a missing person. A 公告 announces a formal decision or rule. One scholar reads 啟 as a hand opening a door.

column3: An email attachment or the appendix of a document: 添加附件, 打开附件, 见附件 for "see attached". It can also be an accessory or extra part of a machine.
column6: Qǐng kàn yóujiàn lǐ de fùjiàn.
column7: Please look at the attachment in the email.
column9: An email attachment or the appendix of a document: 添加附件, 打開附件, 見附件 for "see attached". It can also be an accessory or extra part of a machine.

column3: A pointer that does not say everything, as a verb or a noun: 温馨提示 on signs, 屏幕提示 for an on-screen prompt, 提示音 for an alert sound. It nudges; 提醒 reminds someone of what they know.
column4: 屏幕上出现了一条提示。
column5: 屏幕上出現了一條提示。
column6: Píngmù shàng chūxiàn le yī tiáo tíshì.
column7: A prompt appeared on the screen.
column9: A pointer that does not say everything, as a verb or a noun: 溫馨提示 on signs, 屏幕提示 for an on-screen prompt, 提示音 for an alert sound. It nudges; 提醒 reminds someone of what they know.

column3: A stronger, more official warning than 提醒, with consequences if ignored: 警告他不要…, 受到警告, 严重警告. In sports and games a first warning is 警告.
column4: 老师警告他不要再迟到。
column5: 老師警告他不要再遲到。
column6: Lǎoshī jǐnggào tā bùyào zài chídào.
column7: The teacher warned him not to be late again.
column9: A stronger, more official warning than 提醒, with consequences if ignored: 警告他不要…, 受到警告, 嚴重警告. In sports and games a first warning is 警告.

column3: An instruction from above, as verb or noun: 上级指示, 按照指示, 作出指示. It can also mean to indicate, as a gauge or a signal does: 指示灯 is an indicator light.
column4: 我们要按照领导的指示办事。
column5: 我們要按照領導的指示辦事。
column6: Wǒmen yào ànzhào lǐngdǎo de zhǐshì bànshì.
column7: We must act according to the leader's instructions.
column9: An instruction from above, as verb or noun: 上級指示, 按照指示, 作出指示. It can also mean to indicate, as a gauge or a signal does: 指示燈 is an indicator light.

column3: To pass something from one hand or person to the next: 传递信息, 传递热量, 传递给下一个人. It also carries feelings and messages, such as 传递爱心.
column4: 这个消息很快传递到各地。
column5: 這個消息很快傳遞到各地。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi hěn kuài chuándì dào gèdì.
column7: The news spread quickly to all places.
column9: To pass something from one hand or person to the next: 傳遞信息, 傳遞熱量, 傳遞給下一個人. It also carries feelings and messages, such as 傳遞愛心.

column3: A mailbox, on the street or at home, or a post office box: 邮政信箱. For email, mainland speakers usually say 邮箱, while in Taiwan 信箱 is the everyday word for an email inbox.
column6: Xìnxiāng lǐ yǒu yī fēng xìn.
column7: There is a letter in the mailbox.
column9: A mailbox, on the street or at home, or a post office box: 郵政信箱. For email, mainland speakers usually say 郵箱, while in Taiwan 信箱 is the everyday word for an email inbox.

column3: A fax, both the thing and the act: 发传真, 传真机, 传真号码. Still seen on business cards and forms, though rarer than email.
column6: Qǐng bǎ wénjiàn chuánzhēn gěi wǒ.
column7: Please fax the document to me.
column9: A fax, both the thing and the act: 發傳真, 傳真機, 傳真號碼. Still seen on business cards and forms, though rarer than email.

column3: To send money to someone, often far away or abroad: 银行汇款, 跨境汇款, 汇款单, also done in apps. 转账 just moves money from one account to another. It also names the money sent.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān gěi jiālǐ huìkuǎn le.
column7: I sent money home today.
column9: To send money to someone, often far away or abroad: 銀行匯款, 跨境匯款, 匯款單, also done in apps. 轉帳 just moves money from one account to another. It also names the money sent.

column3: A verb that takes its name or document as the object: 签个名, 签合同. It is also a thin stick or slip, as in 抽签 for drawing lots and 牙签 for a toothpick.
column6: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiān yīxià.
column7: Please sign here.
column9: A verb that takes its name or document as the object: 簽個名, 簽合同. It is also a thin stick or slip, as in 抽籤 for drawing lots and 牙籤 for a toothpick.

column3: To sign your name, or the signature itself: 请在这里签名, 明星签名. It is writing your name as your mark, while 签字 is signing to approve. A chat profile's 个性签名 is a motto.
column6: Zhè wèi gēshǒu gěi fěnsī qiānmíng.
column7: This singer signs autographs for fans.
column9: To sign your name, or the signature itself: 請在這裡簽名, 明星簽名. It is writing your name as your mark, while 簽字 is signing to approve. A chat profile's 個性簽名 is a motto.

column3: To sign to approve or agree: 签字同意, 合同上签字. It is a verb plus object, so the particle goes between: 签了字. 签名 stresses the name itself.
column4: 你签字以后合同就有效了。
column5: 你簽字以後合同就有效了。
column6: Nǐ qiānzì yǐhòu hétong jiù yǒuxiào le.
column7: Once you sign, the contract takes effect.
column9: To sign to approve or agree: 簽字同意, 合同上簽字. It is a verb plus object, so the particle goes between: 簽了字. 簽名 stresses the name itself.

column3: To sign a contract, formal: 签约仪式 is a signing ceremony. It does not take the contract as an object; for that say 签订. It is also how a player or singer signs with a team or label.
column4: 两家公司今天正式签约。
column5: 兩家公司今天正式簽約。
column6: Liǎng jiā gōngsī jīntiān zhèngshì qiānyuē.
column7: The two companies formally signed a contract today.
column9: To sign a contract, formal: 簽約儀式 is a signing ceremony. It does not take the contract as an object; for that say 簽訂. It is also how a player or singer signs with a team or label.

column3: To sign and conclude a treaty, contract or agreement: 签订合同, 签订协议, 签订条约. The object must be the document or deal, while 签约 needs no object. 订 also means to book, as in 订票.
column6: Shuāngfāng qiāndìng le yī fèn hétong.
column7: Both sides signed a contract.
column9: To sign and conclude a treaty, contract or agreement: 簽訂合同, 簽訂協議, 簽訂條約. The object must be the document or deal, while 簽約 needs no object. 訂 also means to book, as in 訂票.

column3: An agreement, in writing or not: 达成协议 "reach an agreement", 签订协议, 和平协议. Also the verb "to agree upon". 协议 stresses that both sides agree; a 合同 "contract" stresses legal rights and duties.
column6: Shuāngfāng zhōngyú dáchéng le xiéyì.
column7: The two sides finally reached an agreement.
column9: An agreement, in writing or not: 達成協議 "reach an agreement", 簽訂協議, 和平協議. Also the verb "to agree upon". 協議 stresses that both sides agree; a 合同 "contract" stresses legal rights and duties.

column3: The written document of an agreement: 签协议书, 一份协议书. 协议 is the agreement itself, and 书 makes it the paper, as in 证书, 说明书 and 保证书.
column6: Tāmen qiān le zhè fèn xiéyìshū.
column7: They signed this written agreement.
column9: The written document of an agreement: 簽協議書, 一份協議書. 協議 is the agreement itself, and 書 makes it the paper, as in 證書, 說明書 and 保證書.

column3: A certificate: 毕业证书, 荣誉证书, 资格证书, 获得证书. A diploma is often just 毕业证, and 证件 means ID papers in general.
column4: 她拿到了英语考试的证书。
column5: 她拿到了英語考試的證書。
column6: Tā ná dào le Yīngyǔ kǎoshì de zhèngshū.
column7: She received the certificate for her English exam.
column9: A certificate: 畢業證書, 榮譽證書, 資格證書, 獲得證書. A diploma is often just 畢業證, and 證件 means ID papers in general.

column3: Formal permission, with an authority giving it: 得到许可, 未经许可 for "without permission", 许可证 for a permit. In speech people say 允许 or 让. Software has a 许可协议 too.
column4: 没有许可，不能进入这里。
column5: 沒有許可，不能進入這裡。
column6: Méiyǒu xǔkě, bù néng jìnrù zhèlǐ.
column7: You cannot enter here without permission.
column9: Formal permission, with an authority giving it: 得到許可, 未經許可 for "without permission", 許可證 for a permit. In speech people say 允許 or 讓. Software has a 許可協議 too.

column3: To register for something: 注册账号, 注册公司, 注册商标, 注册会员. It covers websites, schools and firms alike. 册 began as a picture of bamboo slips strung together.
column4: 你需要先注册一个账号。
column5: 你需要先註冊一個帳號。
column6: Nǐ xūyào xiān zhùcè yī ge zhànghào.
column7: You need to register an account first.
column9: To register for something: 註冊帳號, 註冊公司, 註冊商標, 註冊會員. It covers websites, schools and firms alike. 冊 began as a picture of bamboo slips strung together.

column3: To reach an agreement or result: 达成协议, 达成共识, 达成目标. The object is something abstract, never a place; for a place say 到达.
column4: 经过讨论，大家达成了共识。
column5: 經過討論，大家達成了共識。
column6: Jīngguò tǎolùn, dàjiā dáchéng le gòngshí.
column7: After discussion, everyone reached a consensus.
column9: To reach an agreement or result: 達成協議, 達成共識, 達成目標. The object is something abstract, never a place; for a place say 到達.

column3: A visa: you 申请, 办 or 延期 it, and it comes as 旅游签证, 工作签证 or 学生签证. 签证过期 is an expired visa.
column6: Qù Měiguó xūyào bàn qiānzhèng.
column7: You need to get a visa to go to America.
column9: A visa: you 申請, 辦 or 延期 it, and it comes as 旅遊簽證, 工作簽證 or 學生簽證. 簽證過期 is an expired visa.

column3: To entrust a task to someone: 委托律师, 委托书 is a power of attorney, 受人委托 means on someone's behalf. Pattern: 委托 + person + verb, as in 委托他办理.
column4: 他委托律师处理这件事。
column5: 他委託律師處理這件事。
column6: Tā wěituō lǜshī chǔlǐ zhè jiàn shì.
column7: He entrusted the matter to a lawyer.
column9: To entrust a task to someone: 委託律師, 委託書 is a power of attorney, 受人委託 means on someone's behalf. Pattern: 委託 + person + verb, as in 委託他辦理.

column3: Formal talks between two sides, such as governments, leaders or companies: 举行会谈, 双边会谈. A friendly chat is 聊天, never 会谈.
column4: 两国领导人举行了会谈。
column5: 兩國領導人舉行了會談。
column6: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén jǔxíng le huìtán.
column7: The leaders of the two countries held talks.
column9: Formal talks between two sides, such as governments, leaders or companies: 舉行會談, 雙邊會談. A friendly chat is 聊天, never 會談.

column3: A controversy or dispute: 引起争议, 有争议, 争议很大 "highly disputed", 有争议的话题. Used for a matter on which people disagree openly, in the news and at work. 争 shows two hands pulling at one object. 议 means to discuss.
column4: 这个决定引起了很大的争议。
column5: 這個決定引起了很大的爭議。
column6: Zhège juédìng yǐnqǐ le hěn dà de zhēngyì.
column7: This decision caused a lot of controversy.
column9: A controversy or dispute: 引起爭議, 有爭議, 爭議很大 "highly disputed", 有爭議的話題. Used for a matter on which people disagree openly, in the news and at work. 爭 shows two hands pulling at one object. 議 means to discuss.

column3: To comment on, and a comment: 发表评论 "post a comment", 网友评论 "netizens' comments", 评论员 "commentator". It covers a review of a film, a book, or a news item, and can praise, criticize or neither; 争议 is for disagreement. Both characters have 讠 "speech": 评 "judge" and 论 "discuss".
column4: 很多人在网上评论这件事。
column5: 很多人在網上評論這件事。
column6: Hěn duō rén zài wǎngshàng pínglùn zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Many people are commenting on this online.
column9: To comment on, and a comment: 發表評論 "post a comment", 網友評論 "netizens' comments", 評論員 "commentator". It covers a review of a film, a book, or a news item, and can praise, criticize or neither; 爭議 is for disagreement. Both characters have 言 "speech": 評 "judge" and 論 "discuss".

column3: To assess in a methodical way, with a written result: 风险评估, 评估价值, 对…进行评估. It is more formal and thorough than 估计, which is a rough guess.
column4: 专家正在评估这个项目的风险。
column5: 專家正在評估這個項目的風險。
column6: Zhuānjiā zhèngzài pínggū zhège xiàngmù de fēngxiǎn.
column7: Experts are assessing the risks of this project.
column9: To assess in a methodical way, with a written result: 風險評估, 評估價值, 對…進行評估. It is more formal and thorough than 估計, which is a rough guess.

column3: To release officially: 发布消息, 发布新产品, 新品发布会. Anyone can post online: 发布视频, 发布动态. It makes something public; 发行 puts copies into circulation. 布 means both cloth and “to spread out”.
column4: 公司发布了一款新手机。
column5: 公司發佈了一款新手機。
column6: Gōngsī fābù le yī kuǎn xīn shǒujī.
column7: The company released a new phone.
column9: To release officially: 發佈消息, 發佈新產品, 新品發布會. Anyone can post online: 發佈視頻, 發佈動態. It makes something public; 發行 puts copies into circulation. 佈 means both cloth and “to spread out”.

column3: To issue in quantity into circulation: 发行股票, 发行邮票, 发行新书, and 发行量 is circulation. Compare 发布, which makes something public; 发行 puts copies into circulation: books, stamps, shares, films, albums.
column4: 这本书将在下个月发行。
column5: 這本書將在下個月發行。
column6: Zhè běn shū jiāng zài xià ge yuè fāxíng.
column7: This book will be published next month.
column9: To issue in quantity into circulation: 發行股票, 發行郵票, 發行新書, and 發行量 is circulation. Compare 發布, which makes something public; 發行 puts copies into circulation: books, stamps, shares, films, albums.

column3: A formal word for advocating an idea or cause, often by an organization: 倡导环保, 倡导者. It is more formal than 提倡, and is heard in speeches and reports.
column4: 学校倡导大家少用塑料袋。
column5: 學校倡導大家少用塑膠袋。
column6: Xuéxiào chàngdǎo dàjiā shǎo yòng sùliàodài.
column7: The school encourages everyone to use fewer plastic bags.
column9: A formal word for advocating an idea or cause, often by an organization: 倡導環保, 倡導者. It is more formal than 提倡, and is heard in speeches and reports.

column3: To encourage a practice as a good thing: 提倡节约, 提倡读书, 大力提倡. The subject is usually government, school or society; the object a habit or value. More everyday than 倡导.
column4: 政府提倡大家坐公共交通。
column5: 政府提倡大家坐公共交通。
column6: Zhèngfǔ tíchàng dàjiā zuò gōnggòng jiāotōng.
column7: The government encourages everyone to take public transport.
column9: To encourage a practice as a good thing: 提倡節約, 提倡讀書, 大力提倡. The subject is usually government, school or society; the object a habit or value. More everyday than 倡導.

column3: Communication where both sides come to understand each other: 沟通能力, 和孩子沟通, 有效沟通. It is two-way, not simply sending information, and also used of workplaces and families.
column6: Fùmǔ yào duō hé háizi gōutōng.
column7: Parents should talk with their children more.
column9: Communication where both sides come to understand each other: 溝通能力, 和孩子溝通, 有效溝通. It is two-way, not simply sending information, and also used of workplaces and families.

column3: To get in touch with: 保持联络 "keep in touch", 联络方式 "contact details", 联络员 "liaison". It is somewhat more formal than 联系, which in speech is the usual word on the mainland; in Taiwan 联络 is common in speech. Both characters have a thread or link idea, as 络 has 纟.
column6: Dào le yǐhòu qǐng gēn wǒ liánluò.
column7: Please get in touch with me when you arrive.
column9: To get in touch with: 保持聯絡 "keep in touch", 聯絡方式 "contact details", 聯絡員 "liaison". It is somewhat more formal than 聯繫, which in speech is the usual word on the mainland; in Taiwan 聯絡 is common in speech. Both characters have a thread or link idea, as 絡 has 糹.

column3: An official notice from a government body, school or company: 发布公告, 公告栏 for a bulletin board. A private person posts a 启事 instead. An old explanation, from Han Feizi, reads 公 as the opposite of “private”; one modern scholar disputes it.
column4: 公司在网站上发布了一则公告。
column5: 公司在網站上發布了一則公告。
column6: Gōngsī zài wǎngzhàn shàng fābù le yī zé gōnggào.
column7: The company posted an announcement on its website.
column9: An official notice from a government body, school or company: 發布公告, 公告欄 for a bulletin board. A private person posts a 啟事 instead. An old explanation, from Han Feizi, reads 公 as the opposite of “private”; one modern scholar disputes it.

column3: To analyze: 分析原因, 分析问题, 数据分析. Used as a verb with an object or as a noun, and often with 一下 for a quick look. Both characters mean splitting: 分 separates with a knife and 析 splits wood.
column6: Wǒmen xiān fēnxī yīxià yuányīn.
column7: Let us first analyze the cause.
column9: To analyze: 分析原因, 分析問題, 數據分析. Used as a verb with an object or as a noun, and often with 一下 for a quick look. Both characters mean splitting: 分 separates with a knife and 析 splits wood.

column3: All, without exception: it follows the group it counts and comes before the verb, as in 他们全都来了. It is a little stronger than 都 alone. 全 is built as a whole piece of jade.
column6: Zhèxiē shū wǒ quándōu kànguò.
column7: I have read all of these books.
column9: All, without exception: it follows the group it counts and comes before the verb, as in 他們全都來了. It is a little stronger than 都 alone. 全 is built as a whole piece of jade.

column3: For the most part: 大都是学生, 大都已经离开了. It says most of a group do something, with a few exceptions, and means the same as 大多. For the majority as a noun say 大多数.
column4: 来参加的人大都是学生。
column5: 來參加的人大都是學生。
column6: Lái cānjiā de rén dàdū shì xuésheng.
column7: Most of the people who came were students.
column9: For the most part: 大都是學生, 大都已經離開了. It says most of a group do something, with a few exceptions, and means the same as 大多. For the majority as a noun say 大多數.

column3: The whole world, as a noun or before a verb: 全世界的人, 传遍全世界. 全 + a group works for others too: 全国, 全家, 全班.
column4: 这首歌全世界的人都知道。
column5: 這首歌全世界的人都知道。
column6: Zhè shǒu gē quánshìjiè de rén dōu zhīdào.
column7: People all over the world know this song.
column9: The whole world, as a noun or before a verb: 全世界的人, 傳遍全世界. 全 + a group works for others too: 全國, 全家, 全班.

column3: Numerous, written style, before a noun and only for countable things: 众多游客, 众多原因, 人口众多. Spoken language says 很多. One suggestion is that meat was scarce, so 多 as two pieces of meat meant a lot.
column4: 这座城市有众多的游客。
column5: 這座城市有眾多的遊客。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu zhòngduō de yóukè.
column7: This city has numerous tourists.
column9: Numerous, written style, before a noun and only for countable things: 眾多遊客, 眾多原因, 人口眾多. Spoken language says 很多. One suggestion is that meat was scarce, so 多 as two pieces of meat meant a lot.

column3: Altogether, in reports and notices, placed before the figure: 共计五十人, 共计三千元. Speech uses 一共. 共 began as two hands holding an object up together.
column4: 今天来的客人共计五十人。
column5: 今天來的客人共計五十人。
column6: Jīntiān lái de kèrén gòngjì wǔshí rén.
column7: Altogether fifty guests came today.
column9: Altogether, in reports and notices, placed before the figure: 共計五十人, 共計三千元. Speech uses 一共. 共 began as two hands holding an object up together.

column3: To share something held in common: 共享单车, 共享经济, 资源共享, 共享文件. To give someone a share of what you have is 分享.
column4: 我们和邻居共享一个花园。
column5: 我們和鄰居共享一個花園。
column6: Wǒmen hé línjū gòngxiǎng yī ge huāyuán.
column7: We share a garden with our neighbors.
column9: To share something held in common: 共享單車, 共享經濟, 資源共享, 共享文件. To give someone a share of what you have is 分享.

column3: Overall, as a whole: 总体来说, 总体情况, 总体上看. It opens a sentence with a general view before the details, or comes before a noun.
column4: 总体来说，今年的成绩不错。
column5: 總體來說，今年的成績不錯。
column6: Zǒngtǐ láishuō, jīnnián de chéngjì bùcuò.
column7: On the whole, this year's results are good.
column9: Overall, as a whole: 總體來說, 總體情況, 總體上看. It opens a sentence with a general view before the details, or comes before a noun.

column3: The only one: it comes before the noun, nearly always with 的: 唯一的机会, 唯一的办法. Not the same as 单一, which is "of one kind".
column6: Zhè shì wǒ wéiyī de jīhuì.
column7: This is my only chance.
column9: The only one: it comes before the noun, nearly always with 的: 唯一的機會, 唯一的辦法. Not the same as 單一, which is "of one kind".

column3: Of just one kind, with no variety, and often a weakness: 单一品种, 收入来源单一, 结构单一. Not the same as 唯一, "the only one". It can follow 很.
column6: Tā de shōurù láiyuán hěn dānyī.
column7: He has only one source of income.
column9: Of just one kind, with no variety, and often a weakness: 單一品種, 收入來源單一, 結構單一. Not the same as 唯一, "the only one". It can follow 很.

column3: In storytelling, "all one saw was…": it introduces something sudden, followed by a clause: 只见天上乌云密布. It belongs to narration and fiction, not to everyday report.
column4: 只见他拿起包就跑了出去。
column5: 只見他拿起包就跑了出去。
column6: Zhǐjiàn tā ná qǐ bāo jiù pǎo le chūqù.
column7: All I saw was him grabbing his bag and running out.
column9: In storytelling, "all one saw was…": it introduces something sudden, followed by a clause: 只見天上烏雲密布. It belongs to narration and fiction, not to everyday report.

column3: More than, not limited to: 不止一次, 不止我一个人. After a verb it means without stopping: 笑个不止. For "not only", 不止 and 不只 are often interchangeable; only 不止 has these two uses.
column4: 这本书我看了不止一次。
column5: 這本書我看了不止一次。
column6: Zhè běn shū wǒ kàn le bùzhǐ yī cì.
column7: I have read this book more than once.
column9: More than, not limited to: 不止一次, 不止我一個人. After a verb it means without stopping: 笑個不止. For "not only", 不止 and 不只 are often interchangeable; only 不止 has these two uses.

column3: Follows what was counted: 学生总数, 人口总数. It names the grand figure, as against the parts that make it up. For a sum of money say 总额, and for the sum of several numbers 总和. 数 is shù as a noun here, and shǔ as the verb "to count". 总 is described as literally "to bind together with a rope".
column4: 报名的学生总数超过两千。
column5: 報名的學生總數超過兩千。
column6: Bàomíng de xuésheng zǒngshù chāoguò liǎngqiān.
column7: The total number of students who registered is over two thousand.
column9: Follows what was counted: 學生總數, 人口總數. It names the grand figure, as against the parts that make it up. For a sum of money say 總額, and for the sum of several numbers 總和. 數 is shù as a noun here, and shǔ as the verb "to count". 總 is described as literally "to bind together with a rope".

column3: Paired with a second clause: 除非…否则… names the one condition and what happens without it, and 除非…才… says the result comes only then. 才 marks it as the only way.
column4: 除非你亲自去，否则他不会答应。
column5: 除非你親自去，否則他不會答應。
column6: Chúfēi nǐ qīnzì qù, fǒuzé tā bù huì dāyìng.
column7: Unless you go in person, he will not agree.
column9: Paired with a second clause: 除非…否則… names the one condition and what happens without it, and 除非…才… says the result comes only then. 才 marks it as the only way.

column3: Opens the clause about a case that may not be true, and the main clause usually has 也 or 还: 即使…也…. 就算 says the same in speech, and 哪怕 pictures an extreme case. For a fact that is true, use 虽然.
column6: Jíshǐ xiàyǔ, wǒmen yě yào qù.
column7: Even if it rains, we will go.
column9: Opens the clause about a case that may not be true, and the main clause usually has 也 or 還: 即使…也…. 就算 says the same in speech, and 哪怕 pictures an extreme case. For a fact that is true, use 雖然.

column3: For a fact that is true: the clause after it, often with 但是 or 还是, gives the result that goes against it. A supposed case takes 即使 instead. As a bare invitation, 尽管 plus a verb is "go ahead, don't hold back": 有问题尽管问. 尽 is jǐn in 尽管 but jìn in 尽力.
column4: 尽管很累，他还是坚持工作。
column5: 儘管很累，他還是堅持工作。
column6: Jǐnguǎn hěn lèi, tā háishi jiānchí gōngzuò.
column7: Although he was tired, he kept on working.
column9: For a fact that is true: the clause after it, often with 但是 or 還是, gives the result that goes against it. A supposed case takes 即使 instead. As a bare invitation, 儘管 plus a verb is "go ahead, don't hold back": 有問題儘管問. 儘 is jǐn in 儘管 but jìn in 盡力.

column3: Backs up a view with the fact that settles it, often to defend or forgive: 毕竟他刚来 "after all, he has only just arrived". Comes before the verb or the subject. 竟 alone is a different word, "unexpectedly", as in 竟然.
column6: Tā bìjìng háishi ge háizi.
column7: After all, he is still a child.
column9: Backs up a view with the fact that settles it, often to defend or forgive: 畢竟他剛來 "after all, he has only just arrived". Comes before the verb or the subject. 竟 alone is a different word, "unexpectedly", as in 竟然.

column3: Links choices in a statement, any of which will do: 坐地铁或是打车. 或者 means the same and is the everyday word; 或是 is a bit more written. In a question the word is 还是: 你喝咖啡还是茶?
column4: 你可以坐地铁或是打车。
column5: 你可以坐地鐵或是打車。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zuò dìtiě huòshì dǎchē.
column7: You can take the subway or a taxi.
column9: Links choices in a statement, any of which will do: 坐地鐵或是打車. 或者 means the same and is the everyday word; 或是 is a bit more written. In a question the word is 還是: 你喝咖啡還是茶?

column3: Said twice, it lists options that make no difference: 吃也好，不吃也好 "eat or not, fine". Said once at the end of a remark, it means "that works too, may as well": 这样也好.
column4: 你来也好，不来也好，都没关系。
column5: 你來也好，不來也好，都沒關係。
column6: Nǐ lái yěhǎo, bù lái yěhǎo, dōu méiguānxi.
column7: Whether you come or not, it does not matter.
column9: Said twice, it lists options that make no difference: 吃也好，不吃也好 "eat or not, fine". Said once at the end of a remark, it means "that works too, may as well": 這樣也好.

column3: Marks a result against expectation: 这个办法倒是不错 "this way is good enough, though…". It often concedes a point before a "but". With a command it urges: 你倒是说话呀 "say something already!". 倒 is dǎo when it means to fall, as in 摔倒, and dào here.
column4: 这家店不大，东西倒是挺全的。
column5: 這家店不大，東西倒是挺全的。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn bù dà, dōngxi dàoshi tǐng quán de.
column7: The shop is not big, but it has quite a complete range.
column9: Marks a result against expectation: 這個辦法倒是不錯 "this way is good enough, though…". It often concedes a point before a "but". With a command it urges: 你倒是說話呀 "say something already!". 倒 is dǎo when it means to fall, as in 摔倒, and dào here.

column3: Plays something down: 我只不过开个玩笑 "I was only joking". It ends in 而已 or 罢了 to sound lighter, and is used to defend oneself or to calm a worry. 不过 alone also means "but". 只 is zhǐ here; as a measure word for animals it is zhī, as in 一只猫.
column6: Wǒ zhǐbuguò shì kāi ge wánxiào.
column7: I was only joking.
column9: Plays something down: 我只不過開個玩笑 "I was only joking". It ends in 而已 or 罷了 to sound lighter, and is used to defend oneself or to calm a worry. 不過 alone also means "but". 只 is zhǐ here; as a measure word for animals it is zhī, as in 一只貓.

column3: Points out what is plain, then something that contradicts it follows: 明明知道，却不说. It carries surprise or blame. 显然 only observes that something is obvious, without the reproach.
column4: 他明明知道，却不告诉我。
column5: 他明明知道，卻不告訴我。
column6: Tā míngmíng zhīdào, què bù gàosu wǒ.
column7: He clearly knows, yet he will not tell me.
column9: Points out what is plain, then something that contradicts it follows: 明明知道，卻不說. It carries surprise or blame. 顯然 only observes that something is obvious, without the reproach.

column3: Unexpectedly, surprisingly, with the speaker amazed: 居然忘了 "actually forgot", 居然能… "can even…". It sits before the verb. 竟然 is almost the same. It tells you what the speaker thought would not happen, often bad news.
column4: 他居然忘了自己的生日。
column5: 他居然忘了自己的生日。
column6: Tā jūrán wàng le zìjǐ de shēngrì.
column7: He actually forgot his own birthday.
column9: Unexpectedly, surprisingly, with the speaker amazed: 居然忘了 "actually forgot", 居然能… "can even…". It sits before the verb. 竟然 is almost the same. It tells you what the speaker thought would not happen, often bad news.

column3: A formal word. Before the verb it says no one could doubt it: 无疑会成功. It can close a clause as the predicate: 这一点确定无疑, 这是无疑的. Spoken, people say 肯定 instead. 疑 began as a man with a cane looking around with his mouth open, not knowing where to go.
column6: Zhè wúyí shì ge hǎo xiāoxi.
column7: This is undoubtedly good news.
column9: A formal word. Before the verb it says no one could doubt it: 無疑會成功. It can close a clause as the predicate: 這一點確定無疑, 這是無疑的. Spoken, people say 肯定 instead. 疑 began as a man with a cane looking around with his mouth open, not knowing where to go.

column3: Relief after waiting or trouble: 车总算来了. 终于 can carry relief too, but 总算 adds "at least it came out all right". Only 总算 gives a grudging verdict, "all in all it counts as…": 成绩总算不错.
column4: 等了一个小时，车总算来了。
column5: 等了一個小時，車總算來了。
column6: Děng le yī ge xiǎoshí, chē zǒngsuàn lái le.
column7: After waiting an hour, the bus finally came.
column9: Relief after waiting or trouble: 車總算來了. 終於 can carry relief too, but 總算 adds "at least it came out all right". Only 總算 gives a grudging verdict, "all in all it counts as…": 成績總算不錯.

column3: Before a verb it is "for sure": 他肯定会来. As an adjective it is 肯定的答案, and as a verb it means to approve: 肯定他的成绩. The opposite is 否定. In speech it is a bit stronger than 一定.
column6: Tā kěndìng huì lái de.
column7: He will certainly come.
column9: Before a verb it is "for sure": 他肯定會來. As an adjective it is 肯定的答案, and as a verb it means to approve: 肯定他的成績. The opposite is 否定. In speech it is a bit stronger than 一定.

column3: A firm pledge or refusal, placed right before the verb: 决不放弃, 决不允许. 绝不 says the same. It states a decision, not a plain fact, so it sounds heavy for everyday no's like 我不去.
column6: Wǒ juébù huì fàngqì.
column7: I will never give up.
column9: A firm pledge or refusal, placed right before the verb: 決不放棄, 決不允許. 絕不 says the same. It states a decision, not a plain fact, so it sounds heavy for everyday no's like 我不去.

column3: A spoken guess, based on what you know: 估计要三个小时 "it'll take about three hours". 我估计… softens a prediction. It also covers a rough figure. 评估 is the formal, careful assessment.
column4: 我估计他今天不会来了。
column5: 我估計他今天不會來了。
column6: Wǒ gūjì tā jīntiān bù huì lái le.
column7: I reckon he will not come today.
column9: A spoken guess, based on what you know: 估計要三個小時 "it'll take about three hours". 我估計… softens a prediction. It also covers a rough figure. 評估 is the formal, careful assessment.

column3: A trigger leads to a memory or idea: 由…联想到…, with 到 before what is recalled. Also the noun, as in 自由联想. 想起 is a plain "remember"; 联想 is a link between two things. It is also the brand Lenovo, and 联想输入 is the word prediction of an input method.
column4: 看到这张照片，我联想到小时候。
column5: 看到這張照片，我聯想到小時候。
column6: Kàndào zhè zhāng zhàopiàn, wǒ liánxiǎng dào xiǎoshíhou.
column7: Seeing this photo reminds me of my childhood.
column9: A trigger leads to a memory or idea: 由…聯想到…, with 到 before what is recalled. Also the noun, as in 自由聯想. 想起 is a plain "remember"; 聯想 is a link between two things. It is also the brand Lenovo, and 聯想輸入 is the word prediction of an input method.

column3: Careful, planned imagining, often of a future or a case: 设想一下 "picture this". As a noun it is a plan. 为…设想 means to think things through for someone. 想象 is freer, even fantasy.
column4: 请你设想一下十年后的生活。
column5: 請你設想一下十年後的生活。
column6: Qǐng nǐ shèxiǎng yīxià shí nián hòu de shēnghuó.
column7: Please imagine life ten years from now.
column9: Careful, planned imagining, often of a future or a case: 設想一下 "picture this". As a noun it is a plan. 為…設想 means to think things through for someone. 想象 is freer, even fantasy.

column3: A noun for how the mind works, with set partners: 思维方式, 逻辑思维, 创新思维. It is not a verb: "to think" is 想 or 思考. 想法 is one idea; 思维 is the way of thinking behind them.
column6: Tā de sīwéi fāngshì hěn tèbié.
column7: His way of thinking is very special.
column9: A noun for how the mind works, with set partners: 思維方式, 邏輯思維, 創新思維. It is not a verb: "to think" is 想 or 思考. 想法 is one idea; 思維 is the way of thinking behind them.

column3: As a verb it needs 到: 意识到问题, 没意识到. As a noun it is awareness, and it follows a topic as a pattern: 环保意识, 安全意识, 法律意识. 感觉 is a feeling, 意识 is knowing about it.
column4: 他还没有意识到问题的严重性。
column5: 他還沒有意識到問題的嚴重性。
column6: Tā hái méiyǒu yìshí dào wèntí de yánzhòngxìng.
column7: He still has not realized how serious the problem is.
column9: As a verb it needs 到: 意識到問題, 沒意識到. As a noun it is awareness, and it follows a topic as a pattern: 環保意識, 安全意識, 法律意識. 感覺 is a feeling, 意識 is knowing about it.

column3: The strength to hold to a goal: 意志坚定, 意志力, 钢铁般的意志. It is not the future "will" (that is 会 or 将) and not a wish (愿望). Often in praise, or in the lack of it: 意志薄弱.
column6: Tā yǒu hěn qiáng de yìzhì.
column7: He has a very strong will.
column9: The strength to hold to a goal: 意志堅定, 意志力, 鋼鐵般的意志. It is not the future "will" (that is 會 or 將) and not a wish (願望). Often in praise, or in the lack of it: 意志薄弱.

column3: A conviction one acts on, more than an opinion: 坚定的信念, 失去信念, 坚持信念. 想法 is only an idea. It pairs with 坚定, 动摇, 失去. 念 is described by one scholar as an upside-down mouth over a heart: "to listen to one's heart".
column4: 他始终坚持自己的信念。
column5: 他始終堅持自己的信念。
column6: Tā shǐzhōng jiānchí zìjǐ de xìnniàn.
column7: He has always held to his own beliefs.
column9: A conviction one acts on, more than an opinion: 堅定的信念, 失去信念, 堅持信念. 想法 is only an idea. It pairs with 堅定, 動搖, 失去. 念 is described by one scholar as an upside-down mouth over a heart: "to listen to one's heart".

column3: Two uses. 把A看成B treats A as B: 别把朋友看成敌人. Or a slip of the eye: 把"己"看成了"已". The 把 phrase puts the thing first, and 了 often follows 成. 看 began as a hand held above the eyes to gaze afar.
column6: Bùyào bǎ péngyou kànchéng dírén.
column7: Do not regard your friends as enemies.
column9: Two uses. 把A看成B treats A as B: 別把朋友看成敵人. Or a slip of the eye: 把"己"看成了"已". The 把 phrase puts the thing first, and 了 often follows 成. 看 began as a hand held above the eyes to gaze afar.

column3: Seeing a hidden fact, feeling or quality, not just looking: 我看出他不高兴. The possible forms are everyday: 看得出 "can tell", 看不出 "can't tell". 来 may follow: 看出来.
column4: 我看出他有点儿不高兴。
column5: 我看出他有點兒不高興。
column6: Wǒ kànchū tā yǒudiǎnr bù gāoxìng.
column7: I can see he is a bit unhappy.
column9: Seeing a hidden fact, feeling or quality, not just looking: 我看出他不高興. The possible forms are everyday: 看得出 "can tell", 看不出 "can't tell". 來 may follow: 看出來.

column3: A way of viewing a matter or a person: 如何看待这件事, 正确看待失败. The object is abstract. With a person it takes 把…当…: 把他当朋友看待. It is more formal than 看.
column4: 我们应该正确看待失败。
column5: 我們應該正確看待失敗。
column6: Wǒmen yīnggāi zhèngquè kàndài shībài.
column7: We should look at failure in the right way.
column9: A way of viewing a matter or a person: 如何看待這件事, 正確看待失敗. The object is abstract. With a person it takes 把…當…: 把他當朋友看待. It is more formal than 看.

column3: A written version of 看成 or 当作: 被视为, 视…为…, 视为理所当然. The thing regarded often follows 被 or sits between 视 and 为. 为 is wéi here, and wèi when it means "for" or "because of".
column4: 这种做法被视为不礼貌。
column5: 這種做法被視為不禮貌。
column6: Zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ bèi shìwéi bù lǐmào.
column7: This way of doing it is regarded as impolite.
column9: A written version of 看成 or 當作: 被視為, 視…為…, 視為理所當然. The thing regarded often follows 被 or sits between 視 and 為. 為 is wéi here, and wèi when it means "for" or "because of".

column3: To know by sight: 认字, 认路, 认人. Also to admit: 认错, 认输. Add a complement for recognizing: 认出来. It is also the first character of 认识, 认为 and 认真; for "to know someone" use 认识, not 认 alone.
column4: 他一下子就把我认出来了。
column5: 他一下子就把我認出來了。
column6: Tā yīxiàzi jiù bǎ wǒ rèn chūlái le.
column7: He recognized me right away.
column9: To know by sight: 認字, 認路, 認人. Also to admit: 認錯, 認輸. Add a complement for recognizing: 認出來. It is also the first character of 認識, 認為 and 認真; for "to know someone" use 認識, not 認 alone.

column3: Firmly believing, once and for all: 认定他是对的. It can sound stubborn. In official language it is "to determine": 认定事实, 被认定为.
column6: Tā rèndìng zhè jiàn shì shì duì de.
column7: He is convinced that this is right.
column9: Firmly believing, once and for all: 認定他是對的. It can sound stubborn. In official language it is "to determine": 認定事實, 被認定為.

column3: Based on one's own view, often a mild criticism: 太主观了, 主观想法. Opposite: 客观. It also marks efforts and wishes: 主观努力 "one's own effort", 主观愿望.
column6: Zhè zhǐshì nǐ de zhǔguān xiǎngfǎ.
column7: This is only your own subjective idea.
column9: Based on one's own view, often a mild criticism: 太主觀了, 主觀想法. Opposite: 客觀. It also marks efforts and wishes: 主觀努力 "one's own effort", 主觀願望.

column3: Judgment, mostly in choosing: 有眼光, 眼光独到. Also a viewpoint, as 用发展的眼光看. Literally a look or gaze: 异样的眼光. In the last sense it often follows 用: 用…的眼光看.
column6: Tā mǎi dōngxi hěn yǒu yǎnguāng.
column7: She has a good eye for buying things.
column9: Judgment, mostly in choosing: 有眼光, 眼光獨到. Also a viewpoint, as 用發展的眼光看. Literally a look or gaze: 異樣的眼光. In the last sense it often follows 用: 用…的眼光看.

column3: A casual word for 看: 瞧一瞧, 瞧瞧. 你瞧 draws attention, like "look!". 瞧不起 means to look down on someone, 瞧得起 the opposite. Heard mostly in northern speech.
column6: Nǐ qiáo, nàbiān yǒu yī zhī xiǎoniǎo.
column7: Look, there is a little bird over there.
column9: A casual word for 看: 瞧一瞧, 瞧瞧. 你瞧 draws attention, like "look!". 瞧不起 means to look down on someone, 瞧得起 the opposite. Heard mostly in northern speech.

column3: A steady look, written and a bit literary: 注视着前方. Not a glance, which is 看一眼. The object of attention is often a person, a scene, or developments: 注视事态的发展.
column6: Tā jìngjìng de zhùshì zhe chuāngwài.
column7: He quietly gazed out of the window.
column9: A steady look, written and a bit literary: 注視著前方. Not a glance, which is 看一眼. The object of attention is often a person, a scene, or developments: 注視事態的發展.

column3: To give weight to a quality, with an abstract object: 注重质量, 注重细节, 注重实践. The subject is usually a person or an organization. 重视 is wider: to value and take seriously, also people and problems: 重视人才.
column4: 这家公司很注重产品质量。
column5: 這家公司很注重產品質量。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī hěn zhùzhòng chǎnpǐn zhìliàng.
column7: This company pays great attention to product quality.
column9: To give weight to a quality, with an abstract object: 注重質量, 注重細節, 注重實踐. The subject is usually a person or an organization. 重視 is wider: to value and take seriously, also people and problems: 重視人才.

column3: Looking something up in a system or with an office: 查询成绩, 网上查询, 查询电话. 查 alone is the everyday verb; 查询 is more formal and procedural. The thing looked up can be a record, a number, a status.
column4: 你可以在网上查询成绩。
column5: 你可以在網上查詢成績。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngshàng cháxún chéngjì.
column7: You can check the results online.
column9: Looking something up in a system or with an office: 查詢成績, 網上查詢, 查詢電話. 查 alone is the everyday verb; 查詢 is more formal and procedural. The thing looked up can be a record, a number, a status.

column3: Testing against a standard, with a pass or fail result: 质量检验, 检验合格. 检查 is a general look for problems; 检验 measures. It can be abstract: 实践是检验真理的标准.
column4: 产品出厂前要经过检验。
column5: 產品出廠前要經過檢驗。
column6: Chǎnpǐn chūchǎng qián yào jīngguò jiǎnyàn.
column7: Products have to be inspected before leaving the factory.
column9: Testing against a standard, with a pass or fail result: 質量檢驗, 檢驗合格. 檢查 is a general look for problems; 檢驗 measures. It can be abstract: 實踐是檢驗真理的標準.

column3: To notice something that was already so, often late: 才发觉钥匙不见了. A clause usually follows. Close to 发现, which also covers new discoveries; 发觉 is only a personal realization. 觉 is jué in 发觉 ("to find that"), but jiào in 睡觉.
column4: 回到家，我才发觉钥匙不见了。
column5: 回到家，我才發覺鑰匙不見了。
column6: Huídào jiā, wǒ cái fājué yàoshi bù jiàn le.
column7: Only when I got home did I notice that the key was gone.
column9: To notice something that was already so, often late: 才發覺鑰匙不見了. A clause usually follows. Close to 發現, which also covers new discoveries; 發覺 is only a personal realization. 覺 is jué in 發覺 ("to find that"), but jiào in 睡覺.

column3: A lead to follow in a search: 找到线索, 提供线索, 没有线索. In writing it is also the storyline running through a work: 故事线索. Pair with 破案 for cases and 追踪 for following a trail.
column6: Jǐngchá zhǎodào le xīn de xiànsuǒ.
column7: The police found a new clue.
column9: A lead to follow in a search: 找到線索, 提供線索, 沒有線索. In writing it is also the storyline running through a work: 故事線索. Pair with 破案 for cases and 追蹤 for following a trail.

column3: What really happened, behind appearances: 了解真相, 调查真相, 真相大白. It concerns events and facts, not "true" in general (真 or 真的). 相 is xiàng here, meaning how something appears, and xiāng when it means each other.
column4: 记者终于查出了事情的真相。
column5: 記者終於查出了事情的真相。
column6: Jìzhě zhōngyú chá chū le shìqing de zhēnxiàng.
column7: The reporter finally found out the truth of the matter.
column9: What really happened, behind appearances: 了解真相, 調查真相, 真相大白. It concerns events and facts, not "true" in general (真 or 真的). 相 is xiàng here, meaning how something appears, and xiāng when it means each other.

column3: Confirms a claim that was in doubt: 证实消息, 得到证实, 未经证实. 证明 proves something by reasoning or evidence; 证实 shows it is the case. Often with 被 or in news about reports.
column4: 这个消息已经被证实了。
column5: 這個消息已經被證實了。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi yǐjīng bèi zhèngshí le.
column7: This news has been confirmed.
column9: Confirms a claim that was in doubt: 證實消息, 得到證實, 未經證實. 證明 proves something by reasoning or evidence; 證實 shows it is the case. Often with 被 or in news about reports.

column3: A truth that always holds: 追求真理, 科学真理, 客观真理. It is abstract and large; one fact that happened is 事实 or 真相. "True or false" is 真假.
column4: 科学家一生都在追求真理。
column5: 科學家一生都在追求真理。
column6: Kēxuéjiā yīshēng dōu zài zhuīqiú zhēnlǐ.
column7: Scientists spend their whole lives seeking truth.
column9: A truth that always holds: 追求真理, 科學真理, 客觀真理. It is abstract and large; one fact that happened is 事實 or 真相. "True or false" is 真假.

column3: A formula in math or science: 数学公式, 套公式 "apply a formula". Also a fixed pattern that ignores the case: 办事不能套公式. In the second sense it is often a mild criticism.
column6: Zhège gōngshì hěn nán jì.
column7: This formula is hard to remember.
column9: A formula in math or science: 數學公式, 套公式 "apply a formula". Also a fixed pattern that ignores the case: 辦事不能套公式. In the second sense it is often a mild criticism.

column3: The principle behind how something works: 基本原理, 工作原理, 科学原理. It answers "why does this work?", and 讲原理 means explaining that. Not for a rule you follow, which is 规则. 原 began as a spring bursting from a cliff-side, meaning an origin.
column4: 老师给我们讲了这台机器的原理。
column5: 老師給我們講了這臺機器的原理。
column6: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen jiǎng le zhè tái jīqì de yuánlǐ.
column7: The teacher explained to us the principle of this machine.
column9: The principle behind how something works: 基本原理, 工作原理, 科學原理. It answers "why does this work?", and 講原理 means explaining that. Not for a rule you follow, which is 規則. 原 began as a spring bursting from a cliff-side, meaning an origin.

column3: 逻辑思维 is logical thinking, and 有逻辑 or 没有逻辑 says whether what someone says hangs together.
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn yǒu luóji.
column7: What he says is very logical.
column9: 邏輯思維 is logical thinking, and 有邏輯 or 沒有邏輯 says whether what someone says hangs together.

column3: A regular, organized evaluation with results: 考核员工, 年终考核, 通过考核. Found in companies, schools, official programs. Not a one-off exam (that is 考试). 核 began as a kind of tree, and its "to examine" meaning is linked to the "kernel" sense, "to go to the core".
column4: 公司每年都要考核员工。
column5: 公司每年都要考核員工。
column6: Gōngsī měi nián dōu yào kǎohé yuángōng.
column7: The company assesses its employees every year.
column9: A regular, organized evaluation with results: 考核員工, 年終考核, 通過考核. Found in companies, schools, official programs. Not a one-off exam (that is 考試). 核 began as a kind of tree, and its "to examine" meaning is linked to the "kernel" sense, "to go to the core".

column3: A figure to reach or watch, often set from above: 完成指标, 经济指标, 质量指标. Works as an indicator and as a target. Different from 目标, a goal one picks.
column4: 今年的生产指标已经完成了。
column5: 今年的生產指標已經完成了。
column6: Jīnnián de shēngchǎn zhǐbiāo yǐjīng wánchéng le.
column7: This year's production target has been met.
column9: A figure to reach or watch, often set from above: 完成指標, 經濟指標, 質量指標. Works as an indicator and as a target. Different from 目標, a goal one picks.

column3: Gathers things scattered around: 收集资料, 收集邮票, 收集意见. Both a hobby and a task. For a collector's items it is the usual verb; 搜集 hints at more effort to track things down.
column6: Tā xǐhuan shōují jiù yìngbì.
column7: He likes to collect old coins.
column9: Gathers things scattered around: 收集資料, 收集郵票, 收集意見. Both a hobby and a task. For a collector's items it is the usual verb; 蒐集 hints at more effort to track things down.

column3: The area around a spot: 房子四周, 四周都是山. Place word, so it can sit after 在 or stand alone: 看看四周. 周围 is nearly the same, but takes 的 more: 周围的人.
column6: Fángzi sìzhōu dōu shì shù.
column7: The house is surrounded by trees.
column9: The area around a spot: 房子四周, 四周都是山. Place word, so it can sit after 在 or stand alone: 看看四周. 周圍 is nearly the same, but takes 的 more: 周圍的人.

column3: Whatever is outside a group, an organization or a body: 与外界联系, 外界的影响, 外界环境. The inside is named in the context: a family, a company, a sealed room.
column6: Tā hěn shǎo hé wàijiè liánxì.
column7: He rarely has contact with the outside world.
column9: Whatever is outside a group, an organization or a body: 與外界聯繫, 外界的影響, 外界環境. The inside is named in the context: a family, a company, a sealed room.

column3: The deepest part: 内心深处 "deep in one's heart", 森林深处. X 的深处 follows the place that is deep, and 在…深处 gives the location. 处 is chù, a place, here, and chǔ when it means to deal with, as in 处理.
column6: Tā zǒujìn le sēnlín de shēnchù.
column7: He walked into the depths of the forest.
column9: The deepest part: 內心深處 "deep in one's heart", 森林深處. X 的深處 follows the place that is deep, and 在…深處 gives the location. 處 is chù, a place, here, and chǔ when it means to deal with, as in 處理.

column3: A place far away: 远处传来, 从远处看, 在远处. The opposite is 近处. It is a place word, so it can be a subject or follow 在 and 从.
column4: 远处传来了一阵音乐声。
column5: 遠處傳來了一陣音樂聲。
column6: Yuǎnchù chuánlái le yī zhèn yīnyuè shēng.
column7: A burst of music came from far away.
column9: A place far away: 遠處傳來, 從遠處看, 在遠處. The opposite is 近處. It is a place word, so it can be a subject or follow 在 and 從.

column3: Right near, a colloquial word, said mostly of people: 到他跟前, 孩子在妈妈跟前; also 走到桌子跟前. Also "just before" a date: 年跟前, close to New Year.
column4: 孩子跑到妈妈跟前，抱住了她。
column5: 孩子跑到媽媽跟前，抱住了她。
column6: Háizi pǎo dào māma gēnqián, bàozhù le tā.
column7: The child ran up to its mother and hugged her.
column9: Right near, a colloquial word, said mostly of people: 到他跟前, 孩子在媽媽跟前; also 走到桌子跟前. Also "just before" a date: 年跟前, close to New Year.

column3: To be close to, to approach: 靠近窗户 "near the window", 不要靠近 "do not come near", 靠近我. It takes the object directly. 靠 means to lean against, and 近 has 斤, whose sound (jīn) is near jìn.
column6: Qǐng bùyào kàojìn zhè tiáo hé.
column7: Please do not go near this river.
column9: To be close to, to approach: 靠近窗戶 "near the window", 不要靠近 "do not come near", 靠近我. It takes the object directly. 靠 means to lean against, and 近 has 斤, whose sound (jīn) is near jìn.

column3: The region around a place: 北京一带, 长江一带, 这一带 "around here". After a place name it makes a vague area, without strict borders. 带 shows a belt, so the area is a belt around the place.
column6: Zhè yīdài de jiāotōng hěn fāngbiàn.
column7: Transport around here is very convenient.
column9: The region around a place: 北京一帶, 長江一帶, 這一帶 "around here". After a place name it makes a vague area, without strict borders. 帶 shows a belt, so the area is a belt around the place.

column3: Forward, onward: 向前走, 向前看 "look ahead", 向前迈进 "move forward". It describes direction and also progress, often in a slogan: 勇敢向前. 向 is "toward", 前 "front".
column6: Qǐng xiàngqián zǒu wǔshí mǐ.
column7: Please walk forward fifty meters.
column9: Forward, onward: 向前走, 向前看 "look ahead", 向前邁進 "move forward". It describes direction and also progress, often in a slogan: 勇敢向前. 向 is "toward", 前 "front".

column3: Upward: 向上看, 向上爬 "climb up". It also describes striving for self-improvement: 积极向上 "positive and aspiring", 天天向上. 上 is a short stroke above a long one, the picture of "above", and 下 is the reverse.
column6: Tā táitóu xiàngshàng kàn.
column7: He raised his head and looked up.
column9: Upward: 向上看, 向上爬 "climb up". It also describes striving for self-improvement: 積極向上 "positive and aspiring", 天天向上. 上 is a short stroke above a long one, the picture of "above", and 下 is the reverse.

column3: Up and down. After a number it is "about": 三十岁上下 "around thirty", 一百斤上下. It can mean "all over": 全身上下. In 上下文 it is "context". 左右 is used the same way after a number.
column4: 他三十岁上下，戴着眼镜。
column5: 他三十歲上下，戴著眼鏡。
column6: Tā sānshí suì shàngxià, dàizhe yǎnjìng.
column7: He is about thirty and wears glasses.
column9: Up and down. After a number it is "about": 三十歲上下 "around thirty", 一百斤上下. It can mean "all over": 全身上下. In 上下文 it is "context". 左右 is used the same way after a number.

column3: The place where something is: 所在地 "location", 问题的所在 "where the problem lies", 他所在的公司 "the company he is in". It is a formal noun, after 的 or a verb. 所 shows an axe 斤 at a door 户, and 在 is "be at".
column6: Zhè jiù shì wèntí de suǒzài.
column7: This is where the problem lies.
column9: The place where something is: 所在地 "location", 問題的所在 "where the problem lies", 他所在的公司 "the company he is in". It is a formal noun, after 的 or a verb. 所 shows an axe 斤 at a door 戶, and 在 is "be at".

column3: Inner, intrinsic: 内在美 "inner beauty", 内在联系 "inner connection", 内在动力. It is the opposite of 外在, and used for qualities that are part of the thing itself. 内 is a person entering 冂 a house or frame.
column4: 内在的美比外表更重要。
column5: 內在的美比外表更重要。
column6: Nèizài de měi bǐ wàibiǎo gèng zhòngyào.
column7: Inner beauty matters more than looks.
